title: The Midnight Spire
premise: Oscar Voss, a royal food-taster whose body is a ledger of poisons, secretly keeps accounts for the Guild of Impossible Things, which trades in memories, vanished places, and the last embers of dragon-fire. When a child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Oscar discovers the girl is the living index of a country that was erased from history — and that the guild itself helped erase it. Hunted by the crown's inquisitors and betrayed by her own guildmaster, Oscar must trade away her hard-won immunity, piece by piece, to buy passage through doors that no longer exist. In the end she finds the door out of the dead country, but opening it means choosing between restoring a nation no one remembers and preserving the truth of what the guild did; she chooses truth, letting the last dragon-fire gutter out so the erased can finally be mourned rather than traded.
about_author: Noor Iversen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing documents from nations that no longer appear on maps. They write fantasy about people who keep records of things the world would prefer forgotten.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Oscar Voss tastes the crown prince's dinner and detects hemlock laced with something older than any poison she knows. POV: Oscar. The beat establishes her double life — royal servant by day, guild ledger-keeper by night — and ends on dread as she recognizes the poison's signature from a page she herself recorded.

chapters.title: Ledgers of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: In the guild's cellar archive, Oscar balances accounts of traded memories and bottled sunsets while guildmaster Corvane questions her about the poisoned dish. POV: Oscar. She realizes someone has been reading her ledgers without her seal. Emotional beat: the comfort of order undermined by the first crack of distrust.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: During a storm, a girl of perhaps eight appears at the guild door speaking a language predates kingdoms — a language Oscar finds transcribed in her own oldest ledger. POV: Oscar. The child calls the guildhouse by its name from before the founding. Emotional beat: wonder colliding with guilt.

chapters.title: The Country That Isn't
chapters.summary: Oscar deciphers the ledger page: the child is Ashka, living index of Vellmark, a nation erased by treaty and paid-for forgetting. POV: Oscar, with flashback fragments in Ashka's voice. Corvane orders the child locked in the vault 'for her protection.' Emotional beat: the sick recognition that her own records enabled the erasure.

chapters.title: What the Crown Pays For
chapters.summary: An inquisitor, Dame Halvard, arrives at the palace asking pointed questions about tasters and archives. POV: Halvard. We see the machinery of legal justice bent toward convenient silence, and learn Halvard suspects the guild but serves it too. Emotional beat: menace wearing a lawful face.

chapters.title: Immunity Is a Debt
chapters.summary: Oscar learns the guild's secret: her poison-immunity was purchased, dish by dish, against a future debt — and Corvane intends to collect it by trading her tolerance for the keys to Vellmark's doors. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: betrayal; her own body is collateral she never agreed to spend.

chapters.title: Ashka's Alphabet
chapters.summary: In the vault, Ashka teaches Oscar the pre-kingdom script, and each character Oscar writes costs her a memory of her childhood. POV: alternating Oscar and Ashka. Emotional beat: tenderness deepening into sacrifice — learning the truth literally costs Oscar her past.

chapters.title: The First Door
chapters.summary: Guided by Ashka, Oscar opens a door into a field of ash where Vellmark's capital stood; the air still holds market-day sounds, fading. POV: Oscar. A guild hunter follows them through. Emotional beat: grief made physical — walking through a country's ghost.

chapters.title: Corvane's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Corvane confronts Oscar: restoring Vellmark would unravel every treaty built on its erasure, killing thousands; the guild trades in stability, not justice. POV: Corvane, sympathetic and cold. Emotional beat: the theme sharpened — loyalty to the guild versus truth, with real blood on both sides.

chapters.title: Halvard's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dame Halvard catches Oscar and offers a deal: deliver Ashka and the ledgers, and Halvard will bury the evidence of Oscar's guild work. POV: Halvard, then Oscar. Emotional beat: temptation of safety through complicity; Oscar refuses, and becomes a fugitive.

chapters.title: On the Run Through Borrowed Rooms
chapters.summary: Oscar and Ashka flee through the guild's network of impossible spaces — a staircase that is also a river, an inn that exists on three different nights. POV: Oscar. They grow into true family. Emotional beat: warmth in flight; found family forged under pursuit.

chapters.title: The Dragon Beneath the Ledger
chapters.summary: They reach the guild's deepest vault where the last dragon-fire is kept as the guild's master asset — the flame that burned the records of Vellmark's erasure and now gutters toward death. POV: Oscar. If it dies, everything the fire sealed is unsealed at once. Emotional beat: awe and terror at the story's ticking clock made visible.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: To open the final door out of Vellmark, someone must pay in immunity — the very thing keeping Oscar alive against the crown's poisons. POV: Oscar. She begins paying, dish by dish, memory of taste by memory of taste. Emotional beat: resolve; she chooses the child over her own survival.

chapters.title: What Halvard Remembers
chapters.summary: Halvard, investigating alone, uncovers that she herself was born in Vellmark and her memories were purchased by the crown. POV: Halvard. Her certainty cracks. Emotional beat: the hunter discovering she is among the hunted's stolen kin.

chapters.title: The Guild Turns
chapters.summary: Corvane declares Oscar a thief of guild assets and puts a price on her; old colleagues hunt her through the borrowed rooms. POV: Oscar. A former friend, Maren, lets them escape at terrible cost to himself. Emotional beat: loyalty tested and proven where least expected.

chapters.title: Ashka Speaks
chapters.summary: Ashka reveals she isn't only an index — she chose to become one, volunteering as a child when Vellmark's scholars realized erasure was coming. POV: Ashka, fully hers for the first time. Emotional beat: agency reclaimed; the erased were not passive victims.

chapters.title: The Trial Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Oscar convenes an unlawful tribunal in the ash-field: guild defectors, Halvard, and the fading voices of Vellmark judge Corvane's arithmetic in absentia. POV: ensemble, anchored by Oscar. Emotional beat: justice outside the law — messy, human, and honest about its own cost.

chapters.title: Corvane's Door
chapters.summary: Corvane attempts to open the final door himself and sell Vellmark's restoration to the highest bidder; the half-dead dragon-fire flares at his greed. POV: Corvane. He is consumed not by flame but by every memory he ever brokered. Emotional beat: the trader destroyed by his own inventory.

chapters.title: The Last Dish
chapters.summary: At the door out of Vellmark, Oscar pays her final immunity and tastes, for the first time unprotected, the poison waiting in the threshold — and survives it because Ashka's language, written in her own hand, remakes her. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: transformation; the taster becomes the text.

chapters.title: Guttering
chapters.summary: The dragon-fire falls to an ember. Oscar must choose: feed it Ashka's memories to keep Vellmark alive as a tradable thing, or let it die and set the truth free. POV: Oscar and Ashka together. Emotional beat: the book's central choice, held in a single trembling moment.

chapters.title: Mourning a Nation
chapters.summary: They let the fire go out. Vellmark cannot be restored, but it can be remembered: names read aloud, ledgers opened to the public, Halvard testifying against the crown. POV: ensemble. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into witness; truth chosen over restoration.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: One year later, Oscar runs a school where Ashka teaches the pre-kingdom tongue freely, and the guild's vaults are archives open to all. POV: Oscar, closing frame mirroring chapter one. She tastes an ordinary meal — nothing hidden in it — and writes the first entry of a ledger that records instead of trades. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
